campLines.li: [morning] Light's good, we go out now.
[evening] Hang the meat before it gets dark.
[night] Let the fire burn low, or the game won't come near.
[rain] Rain's washing the trail out, we'll wait.
[snow] Tracks show clean in fresh snow.
[fog] Can't see ten paces, nobody shoots in this.
[winter] The herds come down to the low ground in winter.
[their:lowtech] Wax the bowstring, the damp gets into it.
[their:hightech] Clean the barrel before you sleep.
[back] Same ground as last time, and still good.

farewell.li: The hunters of {FACTION} have packed up their camp {PLACE} and set off after the herds.
[morning] The hunters of {FACTION} broke camp this morning, to make the most of the light.
[night] The hunters of {FACTION} are moving on by night, the way hunters do when the game moves.
[back] The hunters of {FACTION} have packed up {PLACE} again, and say the colony's land is still the best hunting they know.

campLines.li: [child] Are we staying here now?
[child] Can I go over there and look?
[night] Sleep, all of you, I'll keep the fire.
[cold] Everyone closer to the fire.
[rain] Get the bedding under cover.
[morning] Fold the blankets, we keep it tidy here.
[ws:war] We go back when it's quiet, and not before.
[ws:hunger] Little and often, that's how you eat after hungry times.
[ws:sickness] Wash your hands before you eat, every time.
[their:grateful] These people have been good to ours before.

farewell.li: The family from {FACTION} has packed up its camp {PLACE} and set off with everything they own on their backs.
[morning] The family from {FACTION} packed up this morning and set off while the day was young.
[back] The family from {FACTION} has packed up {PLACE} again. {X_nameDef} said the colony is the one place on the road where they can rest.

campLines.li: [morning] First hole of the day, make it a good one.
[evening] Wash the pans before you eat.
[rain] Wet ground digs easy and pans badly.
[their:hightech] Run the detector over that slope again.
[their:lowtech] Bring the sieve, the fine one.
[ws:rush] Everyone and their cousin is out digging this season.
[back] We passed this ground over last time, more fool us.

farewell.li: The prospectors from {FACTION} have packed their picks and pans and set off to try the next hills.
[evening|night] The prospectors from {FACTION} packed up {PLACE} by lamplight and set off, too restless to wait for morning.
[back] The prospectors from {FACTION} have packed up {PLACE} again, still certain the colony's land is hiding something.

campLines.li: [morning] Morning prayers, then we eat.
[evening] Light the lamp, it's time to pray.
[night] Pray quietly, the others are asleep.
[rain] Rain on the road is a blessing too, they say.
[ideology,sameFaith] Here, of all places, they keep our faith.
[ideology,otherFaith] Their faith isn't ours, but they let us pray in peace.
[their:tribal] The spirits of the road walk with us.
[back] Same road, and the same kind hosts.

farewell.li: The pilgrims from {FACTION} have packed up their camp {PLACE} and taken to the road again, toward their shrine.
[ideology] The pilgrims of {IDEO} have set off from {PLACE}, their prayers said and their bedrolls on their backs.
[evening] The pilgrims from {FACTION} set off in the evening, to walk while the day cools.

campLines.li: [morning] Stall's open, come and look.
[evening] Last trade of the day, make me an offer.
[rain] Cover the cloth, quick.
[winter] Furs and blankets are what sells in winter.
[their:medieval] Fair weights and fair measure here.
[their:industrial] Cash or trade, I'm not fussy.
[their:tribal] Bring something to trade, we'll find a match for it.
[back] Same spot as last time, if nobody minds.

farewell.li: The traders from {FACTION} have packed up their stall {PLACE} and set off for the next settlement.
[day] The traders from {FACTION} packed up their stall in the middle of the day and are back on the road.
[back] The traders from {FACTION} have packed up {PLACE} again, and {X_nameDef} said they'll keep the colony as a stop on their road.

campLines.li: [morning] Light the forge, it takes an hour to come up.
[evening] Bank the fire, we'll want it in the morning.
[rain] Keep the charcoal dry, or we're done for the day.
[hot] Forge work on a hot day, there's nothing worse.
[their:industrial] Pass me the file, the fine one.
[their:medieval] Pump the bellows, slow and even.
[back] Same anvil, same spot as before.

farewell.li: The smith from {FACTION} has packed the tools and set off for the next settlement with something to mend.
[evening|night] The smith from {FACTION} let the forge go out at the end of the day's work and set off.
[back] The smith from {FACTION} has packed up {PLACE} again, and said the colony's custom is worth the walk.

campLines.li: [morning] Up before the birds again.
[night,clear] Stars are bright tonight.
[rain] Let it rain, I've a roof.
[snow] Snow keeps the visitors away.
[winter] Wood, more wood, always more wood.
[back] Back again, and you're all still here.

farewell.li: {X_nameDef} has gone from the hut {PLACE}, and left it standing for whoever wants it.
[morning] {X_nameDef} left the hut {PLACE} this morning, with only what {X_pronoun} could carry.
[back] {X_nameDef} has left the hut {PLACE} again, without fuss, the same as last time.

campLines.li: [morning] Line up, the early ones get seen first.
[evening] No more today, come back in the morning.
[cold] Coughs everywhere in this weather.
[their:tribal] The plant does the healing, we only gather it.
[their:hightech] Gloves on, then we look.
[ws:sickness] Cover your mouth when you cough, all of you.
[back] Some of the same faces as last time, that's good to see.

farewell.li: The healers from {FACTION} have packed up their remedies and set off for the next village that needs them.
[evening] The healers from {FACTION} saw their last patient of the day and set off.
[ws:sickness] The healers from {FACTION} have set off from {PLACE}, called on to wherever {SITUATION} is worst.

campLines.li: [morning] Morning hymn first, then we eat.
[evening] Light the candles round the relics.
[night] Someone must always sit with the relics.
[rain] Cover the relics, quickly.
[ideology,sameFaith] Our own faith, here, at the edge of the world.
[ideology,otherFaith] We pray for them too, whatever they keep.
[back] We rested here before, and it was kind to us.

farewell.li: The procession from {FACTION} has lifted its shrine and set off again, the relics carried in front.
[ideology] The faithful of {IDEO} have packed up their camp {PLACE} and taken their relics back to the road.
[morning] The procession from {FACTION} set off this morning with its shrine on its poles.

campLines.li: [evening] Lamps lit, places in a moment.
[morning] Lines, everyone, before breakfast.
[rain] No show in the rain, the paint runs.
[their:tribal] Paint first, then the story.
[their:medieval] The king's speech again, with feeling.
[their:industrial] Someone straighten that curtain.
[back] Same stage, new play, they won't have seen this one.

farewell.li: The players from {FACTION} have packed their costumes and set off for the next town.
[evening] The players from {FACTION} packed up in the evening and set off, saying a stage was waiting for them further on.
[back] The players from {FACTION} have packed up {PLACE} again, and promised the colony a new play next time.

campLines.li: [morning] Sun's low, the shadows are good for sighting.
[fog] Nothing to sight on in this, we wait.
[rain] Keep the sheets dry, all of them.
[their:hightech] Log the bearing and the time.
[their:medieval] Pace it again, and count aloud.
[ws:road] If the new road comes this way, it'll want this valley.
[back] Our old marks are still where we left them.

farewell.li: The surveyors from {FACTION} have pulled up their camp {PLACE} and set off to map the next valley.
[evening] The surveyors from {FACTION} packed up as the light went, their sheets rolled tight.
[back] The surveyors from {FACTION} have packed up {PLACE} again, and the colony's corner of their map is a little more exact.

campLines.li: [morning] Lines in before the sun's on the water.
[evening] Gut them now, before the flies find them.
[rain] They rise in the rain, get your line in.
[cold] Cold water, slow fish.
[hot] Too warm, they've gone deep.
[child] Can I hold the line this time?
[ws:run] The run's on, everybody to the water.
[back] Same pool as last time, and still full.

farewell.li: The fishers from {FACTION} have packed up their lines and baskets and set off along the water.
[animals] The fishers from {FACTION} have packed up {PLACE} and set off, their dog at their heels.
[back] The fishers from {FACTION} have packed up {PLACE} again, and say they'd know this water anywhere now.

campLines.li: [morning] Start on the far wall, it's the loosest.
[evening] Sort the scrap before we eat.
[rain] Cover the good plates, or they'll rust by morning.
[their:lowtech] Old metal's better than new, they knew how to make it.
[their:hightech] Cut along the seam, not through it.
[back] Still plenty left in those old walls.

farewell.li: The salvagers from {FACTION} have loaded what they stripped and set off with it.
[animals] The salvagers from {FACTION} have set off from {PLACE}, their pack beast loaded with old metal.
[back] The salvagers from {FACTION} have packed up {PLACE} again, a little more of the old ruins going with them.

campLines.li: [morning] Out to the rows while it's cool.
[evening] Sharpen the sickles for tomorrow.
[hot] Water first, then another row.
[rain] Wet stalks, mind the blade.
[fall] Get it all in before the frost.
[their:tribal] Sing the harvest song, it keeps the rhythm.
[back] Same fields, same good crop.

farewell.li: The harvest hands from {FACTION} have shouldered their sickles and set off for the next farm.
[evening] The harvest hands from {FACTION} finished at dusk and set off, sickles over their shoulders.
[back] The harvest hands from {FACTION} have packed up {PLACE} again, and said they'll come when the next harvest needs hands.

campLines.li: [morning] Diagnostics first, then breakfast.
[night] The stars are in the wrong places from down here.
[rain] Seal the cells, this rain gets into everything.
[cold] Suit heaters are draining fast.
[ws:wreck] We're not the only ones who came down, are we?
[back] The hull's where we left it, at least.

farewell.li: The spacers from {FACTION} have packed what they stripped from the hull and set off to meet their people.
[night] The spacers from {FACTION} set off by night, sure of their bearing.
[back] The spacers from {FACTION} have packed up {PLACE} again, and left the hull a little lighter than they found it.

campLines.li: [night] Write down the hour, and what you see.
[morning] Nothing in the night, again.
[fog] Can't see it in this fog, write that down too.
[their:tribal] The old ones said stones like this should be watched.
[their:hightech] Note the readings, every hour.
[ws:comet] The comet and the stone, both at once, that's no accident.
[back] It's still here, of course it is.

farewell.li: The watchers from {FACTION} have packed up their camp {PLACE} and turned their backs on the monolith.
[morning] The watchers from {FACTION} packed up after their last night's watch and set off.
[back] The watchers from {FACTION} have packed up {PLACE} again, their notebooks fuller than the last time.

campLines.li: [morning] Water and brush them before anyone comes to look.
[evening] Pen them close tonight.
[hot] Shade for the big one, now.
[cold] Blankets on the thin-coated ones.
[child] Can I lead one in the show?
[ws:fair] They'll want the beasts at the fair, every one of them.
[back] They remember this place, look at them.

farewell.li: The beast show from {FACTION} has packed up its camp {PLACE} and set off for the next town.
[animals] The beast show from {FACTION} has set off from {PLACE}, its animals walking with their keepers.
[back] The beast show from {FACTION} has packed up {PLACE} again, and the keepers say their animals like the colony's ground.

campLines.li: [rematch] We've been practicing since last time.
[beatUs] Your team had our measure, we haven't forgotten.
[beatThem] We'll go easy on you this time, maybe.
[morning] Morning drills, everyone up.
[rain] Some of them love the rain, some hate it.

farewell.li: The trainers of {FACTION} have packed up {PLACE} and set off with their Pokémon for the next town.
[rematch] The trainers of {FACTION} have packed up {PLACE}, already talking about the next rematch.

campLines.li: [morning] Load the beasts while it's cool.
[evening] Water the beasts, then us.
[rain] Salt and rain don't mix, cover the bales.
[hot] Rest the beasts in the heat of the day.
[their:lowtech] Bells on the lead beast, so we hear it in the dark.
[ws:toll] Every toll on the road comes out of the salt price.
[back] Same stop as last time, and glad of it.

farewell.li: The salt caravan from {FACTION} has loaded its beasts and set off down the road with its bales.
[animals] The caravan from {FACTION} has set off from {PLACE}, its beasts loaded with the bales.
[back] The salt caravan from {FACTION} has packed up {PLACE} again, and {X_nameDef} said the colony will stay on its road.

campLines.li: [morning] Lay out the cloth, the best pieces in front.
[evening] The lamps make the silver shine, light them.
[rain] Into the boxes, all of it, the rain spoils the dye.
[cold] In my country it is never this cold.
[hot] This heat is nothing, you should feel ours.
[back] Back again, my friends, and with new things.

farewell.li: The merchants from {FACTION} have packed their wares and set off toward the far markets.
[evening] The merchants from {FACTION} packed up by lamplight and set off, wanting to be well along the road by morning.
[back] The merchants from {FACTION} have packed up {PLACE} again, and {X_nameDef} said the colony is a good stop on a long road.

campLines.li: [morning] Let them graze an hour before we move them.
[evening] Bring them in close for the night.
[night] Easy now, it's only the wind.
[rain] Wet beasts and wet drovers, same as always.
[hot] Water them first, then yourself.
[snow] Keep them moving, or they'll stand and freeze.
[ws:drove] Half the region's herds are on the road this season.
[back] They know this grass, look how they settle.

farewell.li: The drovers from {FACTION} have gathered the herd and set off down the road at a beast's pace.
[animals] The drovers from {FACTION} have set off from {PLACE}, the herd in front and the dog with them.
[back] The drovers from {FACTION} have moved the herd on again, and say the colony's grass is the best on their road.

campLines.li: [morning] Rise, pray, walk.
[evening] Say your wrongs aloud, then sleep.
[rain] The rain is part of the road too.
[cold] Cold is nothing to what we carry.
[ideology,sameFaith] They keep our faith here, they'll understand.
[meme:Guilty] Every step pays back a little of it.
[back] We rested here last time too, and they let us.

farewell.li: The penitents from {FACTION} have taken up their packs and set off again, walking in silence.
[morning] The penitents from {FACTION} set off this morning, as they set off every morning.
[ideology] The penitents of {IDEO} have left their camp {PLACE} to the wind and walked on.

campLines.li: [morning] Sing the waking song to them.
[evening] Sing them to sleep, softly.
[rain] Hear how they drink.
[winter] They sleep in winter, sing quietly.
[ws:drought] They're thirsty, sing them the rain song.
[back] They remember our songs, listen.

farewell.li: The tree-singers from {FACTION} have packed up their camp {PLACE} and gone on to the next grove.
[left:seeds] The tree-singers from {FACTION} have set off, leaving a ring of planted seeds where their fire was.
[evening] The tree-singers from {FACTION} set off in the evening, when they say the trees listen best.

campLines.li: [morning] First one in gets me at my most patient.
[evening] Last one for today, sit down.
[cold] Keep that chest warm, I mean it.
[their:tribal] The plant knows what to do, I only give it to you.
[their:hightech] Swab first, always swab first.
[ws:sickness] I've seen a lot of {SITUATION} on the road this season.
[back] I remember some of your faces from last time.

farewell.li: The traveling healer from {FACTION} has packed the bag and set off for the next village.
[round] The healer from {FACTION} looked in on the colony's sick once more, then packed up and set off.
[back] The healer from {FACTION} has packed up {PLACE} again, and said to send word along the road if anyone needs {X_objective}.

campLines.li: [evening] Tune up, they'll be listening soon.
[morning] Not so loud, it's early.
[rain] Strings hate the damp.
[their:tribal] Drum first, the voices follow.
[their:medieval] Play the old ballad, the one about the river.
[their:industrial] The new one, the one from the city.
[ws:songs] Everyone wants the new song this season, play it again.
[back] Play what we played last time, they'll know it.

farewell.li: The minstrels from {FACTION} have packed their instruments and set off for the next town.
[evening] The minstrels from {FACTION} set off in the evening, with a town ahead that's expecting them, they said.
[back] The minstrels from {FACTION} have packed up {PLACE} again, and promised a new song for next time.

campLines.li: [evening] Light the lamp, it's time.
[night] I'll sit with them tonight.
[rain] Keep them dry, cover them.
[their:tribal] The spirits are waiting for them at home.
[their:medieval] We'll lay them in the churchyard at home.
[ws:mourning] So many on the roads with their dead this season.

farewell.li: The mourners from {FACTION} have taken up their dead and set off for home, walking slowly.
[left:sprig] The mourners from {FACTION} have set off, and the sprig of green planted by the colony's gate is the sign they were here.
[ideology] The mourners of {IDEO} have packed their lamp and walked on with their dead.

campLines.li: [morning] Fresh eyes, start again from the first page.
[evening] Copy it out fair before we sleep.
[night] Lamp, please, and quiet.
[rain] The notes, get the notes under cover.
[their:tribal] The old stories are the real books.
[their:hightech] Check it against the archive copy.
[ws:ruins] The ruins draw everyone this season, we were lucky to get here first.
[back] Last time we missed half of it.

farewell.li: The scholars from {FACTION} have packed their notes tight and set off.
[animals] The scholars from {FACTION} have set off from {PLACE}, their pack beast carrying more paper than food.
[back] The scholars from {FACTION} have packed up {PLACE} again, and say there is still more to learn here.

campLines.li: [morning] Up, everyone, it's a long day.
[evening] Count the seed bags again.
[rain] Good rain for a new field.
[child] Is this where we're going to live?
[their:tribal] The elders chose this land, it will be good to us.
[their:medieval] A new village, and we'll be the first in it.
[foe:mechs] Machines bleed oil, and they still fall.
[foe:hightech] They had better guns, and we still held.
[oldfoe] We've fought them before, and we'll fight them again.
[night] Sleep in your boots tonight.
[hurt] I've had worse, and I'll have worse again.
[their:tribal] The spirits saw us fight well.
[their:medieval] A good day's work for the shield wall.

farewell.li: The war party of {FACTION} has packed up its camp {PLACE} and set off for home.
[morning] The fighters of {FACTION} set off this morning, back to their own people.
[their:tribal] The war band of {FACTION} has gone from {PLACE}, back to their own fires.
[their:medieval] The fighters of {FACTION} have struck their camp {PLACE} and marched for home.

campLines.li: [morning] Walk the road to the bend and back.
[evening] Light at the post, so the road can see it.
[rain] Mud on the road, nobody's moving fast today.
[their:medieval] A road kept is a road traveled.
[their:hightech] Log every party that passes.

farewell.li: The wardens of {FACTION} have packed up their camp {PLACE} and gone back along the road to their people.
[evening] The wardens of {FACTION} packed up at dusk and set off back to their people.

campLines.li: [night] Talk low, voices carry at night.
[morning] Nobody on the road, good.
[rain] Rain covers tracks, that's something.
[ws:war] They'll come looking for us, or they won't.
[their:medieval] I left the banner, and I'm not ashamed of it.
[back] They let us rest last time, and they didn't ask questions.

farewell.li: The deserters have packed up their camp {PLACE} and set off, looking for somewhere nobody knows their faces.
[night] The deserters slipped away from {PLACE} in the dark, as people do who don't want to be followed.
[morning|day] The deserters have packed up {PLACE} and set off, keeping well off the road.
